feedback.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
2{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-2t{y}^{′}+6y=0,\,t>0.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Note that the given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={t}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {t}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}-2t\cdot \lambda {t}^{\lambda -1}+6{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ 2\lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda }-2\lambda {t}^{\lambda }+6{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {t}^{\lambda }[2\lambda (\lambda -1)-2\lambda +6] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2\lambda (\lambda -1)-2\lambda +6 & =0 \\ 2{\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda +6 & =0 \\ 2({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +3) & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +3 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We solve the auxiliary equation by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +3 & =0 \\ ({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +1)-1+3 & =0 \\ (\lambda -1)^{2} & =-2 \\ \lambda -1 & =\pm \sqrt{2}\text{i} \\ \lambda  & =1\pm \sqrt{2}\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the roots are $\lambda =1\pm \sqrt{2}\text{i}.$

Now, we note that

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{1+\sqrt{2}\text{i}} & =t{e}^{\text{i}\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t}=t(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)), \\ {t}^{1-\sqrt{2}\text{i}} & =t{e}^{-\text{i}\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t}=t(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}y(t) & =A{t}^{1+\sqrt{2}\text{i}}+B{t}^{1-\sqrt{2}\text{i}} \\  & =At(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t))+Bt(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)) \\  & =(A+B)t\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)+\text{i}(A-B)t\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can rewrite $y(t)$ as 

$$
y(t)=t({c}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)+{c}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)),
$$

where ${c}_{1}=A+B$ and ${c}_{2}=\text{i}(A-B).$
